reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, post-fix stale re-review batch 4, 2026-08-02

samples_reviewed.question_text: What number is marked on the number line?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency names three units -- ten, hundred, thousand -- but all 6 rounding samples (234, 42, 161, 117, 314, 189) round only to the nearest 10; 'nearest hundred' and 'nearest thousand' are never the stated target unit once.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Across 7 seeds spanning mcq, cloze, and read_mcq, two of the three named sub-cases ('nearest hundred', 'nearest thousand') never appear; only 'Round X to the nearest 10' phrasing is ever generated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Stems like 'Round 314 to the nearest 10.' are short, single-clause imperatives appropriate for grade 3 quarter 1 reading level.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three formatters appear (mcq for 42-46, cloze for 50, read_mcq for 55), but seed 55's variant, 'What number is marked on the number line?', never asks the student to round anything, so it does not add a genuine rounding-task variant.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seed 55 keys option C (the value 59) for simply identifying a marked position, which builds number-line reading rather than the rounding skill this node is meant to teach.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Numbers rounded range only from 42 to 314; nothing in the 7 samples reaches a scale (e.g. a 3-4 digit value with a non-trivial hundreds/thousands digit) where rounding to the nearest hundred or thousand would even be meaningfully distinct from rounding to the nearest ten.
